King of Oceans: The Pacific Ocean is known as the King of Oceans because it is the largest and deepest ocean in the world. It covers the greatest surface area on Earth, holds the highest volume of water, supports major marine biodiversity, and plays a key role in global climate, trade, and marine ecosystems. Since the antipode of any place on the Earth is the place that is diametrically opposite of it, a line drawn from one to the other will pass through the centre of Earth and form a true diameter. [ 5 ] For example, the antipodes of most of New Zealand's North Island lie in Spain. Most of the Earth's land surfaces have ocean at their antipodes; this is a natural consequence of most of the Earth's surface being covered in water.
